A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAHNES and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renamed components and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments on hypergraphs, 3D meshes, and featured graph point clouds, including component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains original FAHNES experiments and adds unfeatured graph benchmark results and coarsening ablations in Section 5 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The core algorithm is retained: hierarchical scale encoding renames node budgets, and explicit masked losses elaborate existing inpainting. A limited reported extension appears in v3 Section 4: optional Dirichlet feature priors and projection for simplex-valued attributes, whereas v2 specifies Gaussian feature priors.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original datasets and adds five unfeatured graph benchmarks: SBM, Tree, Planar, Protein, and household-object point clouds (Appendix E.3). These extend task and domain coverage; the ordinary SBM and Tree graphs are distinct from the retained hypergraph datasets.

E2.justification: Mesh comparisons expand from the sequential baseline alone to include WGAN, Flow Matching, and VAE (Table 7 in both versions). v3 also introduces reported graph comparisons with HSpectre and BwR. Its Table 3 adds a Flow Matching OOM entry for featured point clouds, although Appendix Table 9 omits that row.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix D specifies 25 sampling steps throughout; v3 Appendix E specifies 256 for unfeatured hypergraphs and featured point clouds, retaining 25 for meshes. v3 also introduces coverage/diversity metrics, protocols for the added graph benchmarks, and 100-epoch training for new mesh baselines. The sampling-budget revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original budget/OT ablations remain, including those moved out of the main text. v3 adds a focused comparison of random, feature-preserving, and spectrum-preserving coarsening on both mesh categories (Table 12), and extends existing mesh ablations with coverage/diversity measurements.

E5.justification: v3 Table 7 first supplies uncertainty for the existing sequential mesh baseline, which had point estimates in v2. Both appendices already define reported uncertainty as twice the standard deviation over five runs; no increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds graph benchmark results, mesh comparator outcomes, coverage/diversity scores, and coarsening results. In appendix Table 7, sequential ChamDist changes from 0.143 to 0.082±0.074 for Airplane and from 0.117 to 0.169±0.007 for Bench. Corresponding FAHNES values remain 0.048±0.003 and 0.064±0.005; most original FAHNES results are retained.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the shorter-path proposition with a displacement-variance reduction proposition and proof, and adds a gradient-signal proposition and proof (Appendices B.2–B.3). It also revises total generation complexity from O(n+m+k) to O((n+m+k) log n), comparing v2 Appendix G with v3 Appendix H.

C1.justification: The central claim of scalable hierarchical joint topology/feature generation for graphs and hypergraphs remains. v3 tempers the abstract's state-of-the-art claim to competitive or state-of-the-art performance, explicitly emphasizes quasi-linear complexity, and adds a claimed gradient-signal benefit to the conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 adds the explanation that stationary regions dominate the learning objective and that masking preserves useful refinement gradients (Section 4). It also extends the mesh interpretation to comparisons with naive joint generators. Limitations concerning large structures, richer attributes, and computational expense remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an open-source code link, AdamW and its learning rate, Heun integration, dataset-specific spectral or random conditioning details, explicit loss masks, and parameter counts and training instructions for new mesh baselines. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v2.

R1.justification: Related work adds hierarchical molecular generators, including MolGrow, MolHF, and Qiang et al., distinguishing FAHNES through domain generality and scalability. Additional references support WGAN, BwR, and graph datasets. This is a focused expansion of the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and terminology changes throughout. Implementation becomes a dedicated Section 4, the probabilistic derivation moves into a new Appendix A, and the remaining sections and appendices are reorganized. Impact and acknowledgment statements are also added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Hypergraph summary tables are merged, graph and mesh comparison tables are added, and ablation displays and metric columns are reorganized. Figure 3 gains point-cloud coarsening sequences, while the final appendix adds graph-generation visualizations.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's limited comparative evidence by adding several joint mesh generators and scored comparisons on five unfeatured graph benchmarks. Coverage/diversity measurements, coarsening controls, and fuller implementation documentation make the framework easier to assess and reproduce. The unexplained sampling-budget revision and discrepancies between some summary and appendix values remain weaknesses, but the expanded evidence resolves important evaluation gaps and provides a clear overall gain.
